name: Shipping & Trading
pullQuote: Cargo moves on relationships as much as on routes, and relationships take longer to build.
overview: The shipping and trading business moves bulk and liquid cargo across the group's markets. It is the sector where the group's international reach is most literal, and the one most exposed to conditions nobody controls — weather, congestion, and a market that can reprice between agreeing a cargo and loading it.

Trading and shipping are run as one thought rather than two. A cargo that is well bought and badly moved is not a good cargo, so the operational side of the business is treated as part of the commercial decision rather than a consequence of it.

approach.heading: Reliability when nothing agrees
body: Conditions at sea and conditions in the market rarely cooperate, and the useful skill is being predictable to a counterparty when neither is going the right way. The group would rather be the party that turns up on the agreed terms in a bad month than the one that optimised a good one.

That produces a bias towards fewer, longer relationships. Repeat counterparties know how the group behaves under pressure, which removes a category of risk from both sides and is worth more over time than a better rate taken once.
